clue.text: It goes round and around as well as up and down

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters read the same going up the column as going down it

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that spins and also goes up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up and down' says the answer reads the same in both directions, which in a down light means bottom to top as well as top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the spinning part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blades.

clue.text: European of average or lower reputation

parts.note: de is the word for 'of' in French and several other European languages
mean is the arithmetical average

explanation.surface: Someone from Europe of middling or poor standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European of' is a single piece: the European word meaning 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to degrade them, cutting their standing.

clue.text: Loft houses local area with an expanse of water

indicators.note: the loft word holds the local area letters inside, as a house holds occupants

parts.note: a loft is an attic
LAN stands for local area network

explanation.surface: An attic flat housing a local network, with a view over the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic is the ocean between Europe and the Americas.

clue.text: Guesthouse next to an inn with a following

indicators.note: the a comes after the inn word, following it

parts.note: a tavern is an inn

explanation.surface: A guesthouse beside a pub that has a loyal clientele.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' looks like a noun for a crowd of fans but tells you the A goes after.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverna is a small Greek inn or eating place, sometimes offering rooms.

clue.text: Smashing do, catered for and honoured

indicators.note: smashing breaks the letters of do and catered up to be put together again

explanation.surface: A great party, with catering, held for someone honoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' reads as 'excellent' praising the do, but it signals the anagram of DO and CATERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone decorated has been given a medal or award, so honoured.

clue.text: In need of construction, so made the house

indicators.note: the letters of so made the still have to be built into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something needed building, so they made the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A homestead is a farmhouse with its surrounding land.

clue.text: British farthing that is in use at the bar

indicators.note: the that-is letters go inside the British and farthing letters

parts.note: f was the abbreviation for the farthing, an old British quarter-penny coin
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A British coin that is still used in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the bar' looks like a pub, but it is the legal profession; a farthing was an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief is the case papers given to a barrister, the tool of the court advocate's trade.

clue.text: Knight came up to him with food

indicators.note: in a down clue the knight's title rises, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Sir is a knight's title
Otto stands for a man, a typical crossword male name

explanation.surface: A knight approached a man carrying something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'him' stands for a man's name, here Otto.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish.

clue.text: Spruce up enamel containers

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom letter of the containers word moves up to the top

parts.note: enamel mugs are metal cups coated in enamel

explanation.surface: An instruction to tidy up some enamel pots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spruce up' reads as one phrase, but 'Spruce' alone is the definition and 'up' lifts the final S of MUGS to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug in its older sense means neat and trim in dress.

clue.text: Perform work with energy and speed

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
E is the physics symbol for energy
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: Doing a job briskly and vigorously.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to work or function, as a machine performs.

clue.text: To mother, northerner could bring luck

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
a Scot comes from the north of Britain

explanation.surface: Advice that marrying a Scot might be lucky for a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object kept as a lucky charm.

clue.text: One wearing a college shirt

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
T stands for a T-shirt

explanation.surface: A student dressed in a university sweatshirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, the number one.

clue.text: Last event of the day under the cover of darkness

parts.note: night is the time of darkness
a cap covers the head

explanation.surface: Something final happening secretly at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under the cover of darkness' reads as secrecy, but it is literally a cover (cap) for darkness (night).
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is a final drink before bed, or the last race or game of a day.

clue.text: Nut consumed at teatime!

explanation.surface: A nut eaten with afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruitcake is slang for a crazy person, a nut, and also a cake eaten with tea.

clue.text: Counter distressing rebuke

indicators.note: distressing knocks the letters of counter out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: Responding to an upsetting telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to beat soundly or, in an older sense, to scold severely.

clue.text: Outshine at university theatre

parts.note: up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford
the stage stands for the theatre

explanation.surface: Doing better than everyone at a college drama.
explanation.definitionFit: To upstage someone is to draw attention away from them, eclipsing them.

clue.text: Turned on by Greek character who expressed choice

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a person who voted expressed a preference

explanation.surface: A Greek is attracted by someone who made a choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned on' suggests arousal, but means rotated on a pivot.
explanation.definitionFit: Pivoted means swung round on a central point or axis.

clue.text: Dedicate to a trendy calligrapher

parts.note: in means fashionable
a scribe is one who writes by hand

explanation.surface: Asking a fashionable calligrapher to write a dedication.
explanation.definitionFit: To inscribe a book is to write a dedication in it.

clue.text: Water feature of the Tay and ure's meandering

indicators.note: the letters of the two river names wander about like a winding river

explanation.surface: Describing where the rivers Tay and Ure wind down to the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay and the Ure are rivers in Scotland and Yorkshire; 'meandering' fits them but rearranges TAY and URES.
explanation.definitionFit: An estuary is the tidal mouth of a river.

clue.text: Fail to reach ten new sisters beginning their errands

parts.note: to miss is to fail to reach
IO looks like the figures one and zero, ten

indicators.note: only the start of the sisters word is used

explanation.surface: Ten novice nuns failing to make it as they set off on tasks.
explanation.definitionFit: Missions are tasks one is sent out to perform.

clue.text: Decoration used in printing a sign

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, an honour
an en is a printers' measure of width

explanation.surface: An ornament found in printed signs.
explanation.walkthrough: The OM is the Order of Merit, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent, a sign of things to come.

clue.text: Mark left by sectioning an insidious carbuncle

indicators.note: cutting a section out of the words reveals the letters across their join

explanation.surface: A surgeon's cut through a nasty boil leaves a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the mark a healed wound leaves on skin.

clue.text: Feel sublime in the summer

explanation.surface: Feeling wonderful in summertime.
explanation.definitionFit: August means grand and majestic, and it is also the late-summer month.

clue.text: Swagger in a groove on the way

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
a rut is a groove

explanation.surface: Walking cockily along the road, stuck in a routine.
explanation.definitionFit: To strut is to walk in a proud, showy manner.

clue.text: Abrasion caused by clumsy capers

indicators.note: clumsy treatment knocks the letters of capers into disorder

explanation.surface: A graze from some awkward high jinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is a graze, a skin injury from rubbing.

clue.text: Thoroughly appropriate vertical instrument

parts.note: up means completely, as in eat up or use up
right means suitable

explanation.surface: Praise for a well-suited piano.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright is a piano with its strings set vertically.

clue.text: Heavens above! Glides over the earth

indicators.note: the glides word goes over, that is around, the earth letter

parts.note: skis means glides on snow

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone gliding high above the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavens above!' sounds like an exclamation, but it is the literal sky overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: The skies are the heavens overhead.

clue.text: Could this artistic design be a square, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that be and a square might be rearranged

explanation.surface: A question whether a decorative pattern might be square.
explanation.definitionFit: An arabesque is an ornate design of interlaced flowing lines.
